title: 1D DP: take or skip
summary: Largest sum of nonnegative values with no two adjacent. dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + values[i]), rolled into two variables. O(n) time, O(1) space.
code: # Choose between skipping this value and taking it.
triggers: maximize, minimize or count over choices where taking one blocks its neighbour
a recursion that recomputes the same prefix or suffix
prompts: A runner may train on any day but never two days in a row, and each day's session has a fitness score. Maximize the total score.
Billboard slots along a road each pay a fee, but neighbouring slots can't both be rented. Choose slots to maximize income.
invariant: After each value, previous_one is the best total for the prefix so far and previous_two the best for the prefix one shorter.
mantra: Take it plus two back, or skip it and keep one back.
pitfalls: Shift previous_two before overwriting previous_one, or use a tuple assignment.
Write the full recurrence and base case first, then roll the table into variables.
If at least one value must be taken, the empty-choice base of 0 is wrong for all-negative input.

anchors.name: House Robber II
anchors.trick: Circular street: best of values[1:] and values[:-1].

anchors.name: Climbing Stairs
anchors.trick: Same two-variable roll with + instead of max.

mutations.explanation: Adds value to a total that may already include its neighbour.
Both variables end up holding dp[i], so the next value is added next to its neighbour.
